summary: Google has open-sourced Scion, a multi-agent orchestration testbed framed as a 'hypervisor for agents'. It manages concurrent deep agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenCode) across containers, VMs, and Kubernetes with isolated identity, credentials, and git worktrees per agent. Design philosophy: 'isolation over constraints' — agents run in --yolo mode with boundaries enforced at the infrastructure layer (containers + network policy) rather than via in-context behavioral rules. Orthogonal modules for agent memory, chatrooms, and task management. Demonstrated via Relics of the Athenaeum, a multi-agent puzzle game.
key_takeaways: 'Hypervisor for agents' framing — Scion schedules agents as workloads across local/VM/Kubernetes with isolated credentials and shared workspaces
'Isolation over constraints' design philosophy — agents run in --yolo mode, boundaries enforced at infrastructure layer not prompt layer
Harness-agnostic AgentHarness adapter model — full Claude Code + Gemini support, partial OpenCode + Codex
Agent memory, chatrooms, and task management shipped as orthogonal composable modules, not a monolithic framework
Google uses an interactive multi-agent game (Relics of the Athenaeum) as its demo/eval harness instead of static benchmarks

cross_references.connection: Scion's 'isolation over constraints' philosophy and container+worktree+network-policy pattern is the infrastructure-layer counterpart to Sunil Pai's Deno capability-bounded worker sandbox (Code Mode) from AIE Europe 2026 — same goal, different layer
Scion uses Claude Code as a first-class supported harness via its AgentHarness adapter
Overstory's AgentRuntime adapter + merge queue is the closest pattern match to Scion's AgentHarness adapter model
Gas Town's git worktree isolation + actor model is the tmux-level ancestor of Scion's container-level isolation
Scion's orthogonal memory/chatroom/task modules mirror the 12-Factor Agents deconstruction philosophy

notes_for_burak: External validation from Google of the exact architecture we've converged on (tmux+worktree+isolated credentials). 'Isolation over constraints' in four words IS our operating philosophy. Worth reading the Scion source carefully for: (1) AgentHarness adapter abstraction — directly transferable to our orchestrator; (2) network policy enforcement pattern — candidate replacement for --dangerously-skip-permissions; (3) chatroom module — reference for L-Thread agent-to-agent messaging. Not a drop-in replacement (GCP-centric) but a top-tier reference architecture.
